title: How to Measure an HVAC Filter for the Right Size
h1: How Do You Measure and Find the Right HVAC Filter Size?
description: Not sure what size air filter your system takes? Learn how to read the filter label, measure it yourself, and why a snug fit matters for clean, healthy air.
quick_answer: Check the size printed on the edge of your current filter, listed as length by width by depth in inches. If there's no label, measure the filter or the filter slot with a tape measure. Filters are sold by a rounded nominal size, so the actual size is usually slightly smaller. The filter should fit snugly with no gaps.
body:
Buying the wrong filter size is one of the most common HVAC mistakes we see. A filter that's too small leaves gaps where dust slips right past it. One that's too big gets bent or forced in, which leaves gaps too. Getting the right size takes a few minutes.

Where is your HVAC filter?

Before you can measure it, you need to find it. Common spots in Southern California homes:

  • A return grille in a hallway ceiling or wall, behind a hinged cover
  • A slot at the furnace or air handler in a garage, hall closet or attic
  • A filter cabinet next to the furnace that holds a thicker media filter

Some homes have more than one return grille, each with its own filter. Check every return, because they may be different sizes. While you're there, note how easy each one is to reach, since a filter that's hard to get to is the one most likely to be forgotten.

How do you read the size on your filter?

Most filters have the size printed on the cardboard frame, something like 16 x 25 x 1. The numbers are length, width and depth in inches. Write it down or snap a photo before you shop.

That printed number is the nominal size, which is rounded up for convenience. The actual size is usually about half an inch smaller in length and width, so a 16 x 25 x 1 filter might really measure 15.5 x 24.5 x 0.75. That's normal. Stores sell filters by nominal size.

How do you measure a filter without a label?

  1. Turn the system off at the thermostat.
  2. Remove the old filter and lay it flat.
  3. Measure the length and width with a tape measure, to the nearest quarter inch.
  4. Measure the depth, or thickness, of the frame.
  5. Round each measurement up to the nearest whole inch to get the nominal size. Depth is the exception: a frame just under 1 inch is a 1-inch filter.

If there's no filter at all, measure the opening or slot instead, then subtract a little so the new filter slides in without forcing it.

Does filter thickness matter?

Yes. The depth has to match what the slot or cabinet is built for. A 1-inch filter in a 4-inch cabinet leaves a big gap for air to go around. Common depths are 1, 2, 4 and 5 inches.

Thicker media filters have more surface area, so they can trap more without restricting airflow as much, and they last longer between changes. If you're interested in better filtration for allergies or wildfire smoke, a media filter cabinet is often a good upgrade. Our HVAC team can tell you if your system is a good candidate.

Which MERV rating should you choose?

MERV ratings tell you how well a filter catches particles. Higher numbers catch smaller particles.

MERVWhat it catchesGood for
1-4Large dust and lintBasic equipment protection
8Dust, pollen, mold sporesMost homes
11Finer dust and pet danderPets and mild allergies
13Fine particles including much of the smokeAllergies and wildfire season, if the system can handle it

Higher-rated filters can restrict airflow on some systems. If you notice weaker airflow or the system running longer after switching, ask a technician to check.

Which way does the filter go in?

Look for the arrow printed on the frame. It shows the direction of airflow and should point toward the furnace or air handler, away from the return grille. In a ceiling return, that usually means the arrow points up into the ceiling. A filter installed backward doesn't filter as well and can get pulled out of shape.

What happens if the filter doesn't fit right?

Gaps around the filter let unfiltered air go straight to the blower and coil. Over time that dust coats the coil, cuts efficiency and feeds mold. If your filter slot has gaps even with the right size, foam weatherstripping or a better filter rack can close them.
faqs: What does 16x25x1 mean on an air filter?
It's the nominal size in inches: 16 long, 25 wide and 1 deep. The actual measured size is usually a bit smaller, which is normal.
Can I use a slightly smaller filter?
It's not a good idea. Even small gaps let air bypass the filter and carry dust into the system. Use the correct size, and close any gaps with a proper filter rack or seal.
Why does my house have more than one filter?
Many homes have several return grilles, each with its own filter, or a filter at both the return and the furnace. Check and change each one.
How often should I replace my HVAC filter?
Every one to three months for 1-inch filters. Thicker media filters often last six months or more. Check more often during wildfire smoke or if you have pets.
